newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-WEARY BECKER TAKES FIRST TITLE SINCE INJURY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WEARY BECKER TAKES FIRST TITLE SINCE INJURY.

text.p: A weary Boris Becker needed four sets to beat Jan Siemerink of the Netherlands at the $800,000 CA Trophy on Sunday and win his first title since injuring his wrist at Wimbledon.

Although fifth-seeded Becker was far from his best form he won 6-4 6-7 6-2 6-3 on the indoor hardcourts at Vienna's Stadthalle for his 47th career title and third of the year after the Australian Open and Queens.
The victory which levelled the head-to-head between the pair to 2-2, came as a relief for Becker, who took a long break after tearing a right wrist ligament in a third round match at Wimbledon.
He returned to the circuit last month but recurring wrist troubles saw him pull out in the first round in Bucharest, lose in the second round in Basel and withdraw from Lyon last week.
The 28-year-old will make his next appearance at the Czech indoor open in Ostrava next week where his first round opponent is Denmark's Federick Fetterlein.
World number seven Becker had a good start, planting a forehand on the line to convert his second break chance for a quick lead in the opening game.
His left-handed opponent failed to capitilise on four break points in the following game, and the German went on to clinch the set.

The match lost momentum in the second set when games went with serves into a tiebreak. Both player's missed a set point each until Siemerink profited from a backhand from Becker which went wide for 9-7.
The German had difficulties holding his serve in the opening game of the third set but stepped up a gear to break and edge ahead 3-1 with a thundering backhand return.
Siemerink again dropped serve and Becker clinched the set with a low forehand return.
In the fourth, Becker needed a single break for 5-3 to serve for victory after two hours and 38 minutes.
A visibly emotional Becker stuttered badly while thanking his entourage after accepting the trophy.
